summary: SSH agent SSO signer not forwarding CA to proxy, causing git and dashboard auth failures
description:
Issue summary:
Several engineers report failing to clone/pull private repos and being unable to open Grafana dashboards. Errors surface as SSH auth failures against the internal SSH proxy and 403s in the console. Problem started after an Okta device-trust client update rolled on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- Multiple developer workflows blocked (git clone/push).
- On-call engineers cannot access Grafana runbooks tied to incidents.
- Productivity impact across two teams (Infra and SDK).

Environment:
- prod-us-west (SSH gateway cluster sgw-prod-3)
- Okta device-trust release v2.8.1 deployed 2026-03-09

Observed errors:
- ssh: handshake failed: no acceptable authentication methods
- logs show proxy rejecting agent-signer assertion: "missing CA-forwarding-claim"
- Grafana requests 403 with SSO error: "assertion missing forwarding_subject"

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start local ssh-agent and add key using okta-ssh-sign (okta-signer v1.5.0).
2) Attempt git clone git@git.internal.redwood.ai:team/repo.git from a laptop with device-trust enrolled.
3) Observe immediate failure and check ssh-agent debug output.

Notes: This is not a full outage but blocks core developer flows. The condition appears intermittent across machines; some users on the same Okta policy are unaffected (likely dependent on agent version and agent-forwarding negotiation).
steps_to_reproduce: Start ssh-agent and add key via okta-ssh-sign: okta-ssh-sign --ttl=8h ~/.ssh/id_rsa
Observe: ssh failure and proxy logs showing 'missing CA-forwarding-claim'
logs: 2026-03-10T09:12:33Z sgw-prod-3 authz: reject assertion uid=liam: missing CA-forwarding-claim
ssh-agent: agent_sign_request: signing failed: agent refused operation
grafana: sso: assertion validation failed: forwarding_subject not present
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:20 - Replicated with okta-signer v1.5.0 inside a corporate laptop image; agent did not include claim 'ca_forward'.
03/10 10:02 - Confirmed ssh-gateway code checks for 'ca_forward' in Okta assertion before issuing proxy cert; behavior introduced by recent proxy hardening (PR #5128).
03/10 11:15 - Not all users impacted: machines running okta-signer v1.4.3 still forward claim (suggests signer change in 1.5.0).
03/10 12:05 - Reproduced 100% when using okta-signer 1.5.0 + device-trust v2.8.1; downgrade to signer 1.4.3 restores functionality.

03/11 08:30 - Reached out to Identity Eng (@Maya Thompson) and Gateway Eng (@Ravi Patel) on #internalsso. Identity flagged a changed default in signer that now omits ca_forward unless explicit flag provided.
workaround: Instruct affected engineers to downgrade okta-signer to v1.4.3 or re-run okta-ssh-sign with --forward-ca flag (okta-signer v1.5.0+). Applied temporary developer guidance in #support-internal. Onboarding note: desktop provisioning image pinned to 1.4.3 until fix.
resolution: Ongoing - Identity Eng to release signer patch that re-enables CA forwarding by default or exposes clearer UX. Gateway Eng will deploy a compatibility toggle to accept assertions without ca_forward for one week to reduce impact. Follow-up: automated integration test to prevent regression.
next_steps: Identity Eng to cut hotfix for okta-signer (target 2026-03-13)
Gateway Eng to enable compatibility toggle in sgw-prod-3 (target 2026-03-13) and monitor for auth error rate drop
Communicate permanent fix and recommend signer upgrade path to all engineers via #internal-tools and developer weekly
Add integration test covering ca_forward claim in CI for ssh-gateway repository

2026-03-10 10:10 - Liam O'Connor: Pasted outputs above in 'logs' section. Verified downgrade to 1.4.3 works on my laptop.
2026-03-10 11:40 - Maya Thompson (Identity Eng): Confirmed change in 1.5.0. We're preparing a 1.5.1 patch to restore ca_forward by default. ETA EOD 2026-03-12.

2026-03-11 08:47 - Ravi Patel (Gateway Eng): Adding a short-lived guard in ssh-gateway to accept assertion when ca_forward is missing for agent-signer v1.5.x. Will ship canary to prod-us-west later today.
2026-03-12 09:05 - Evan Liang: Canary deployed to sgw-prod-3; initial metric: auth rejects down from 12/min -> 1/min. Keep monitoring and collect impacted user list for postmortem.
2026-03-12 17:20 - Liam O'Connor: Workaround successful for my team. Please advise once Identity releases the patch so we can re-upgrade.
2026-03-12 18:00 - Maya Thompson: Patch v1.5.1 published to internal package registry. Announcing rollout and recommending users update.
